summary.tldr: Lets courts order offenders to do rehabilitation measures in custody, and requires parole decisions to consider progress on those measures; also adds a sentencing factor for large-scale fentanyl trafficking.
what_it_does: Allows courts to order offenders, along with jail time, to take steps during custody such as job training, approved treatment, writing to victims, or other measures the court sets.
Requires offenders to make reasonable efforts to complete any court-ordered measures within the time set by the court.
Requires courts to send the Correctional Service of Canada information about any court-ordered measures.
Requires correctional plans and program planning to take court-ordered measures into account, and requires parole boards to consider reports on progress with those measures.
Requires sentencing courts to treat trafficking in fentanyl in quantities that show large-scale trafficking as an aggravating factor.
summary.background: The bill adds section 729.2 to the Criminal Code and makes related changes to the Corrections and Conditional Release Act and the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act.
